title: heist ticket show lists the code plan and the relations
description: In bin/heist.js the function ticketText prints a ticket as a document: the sections of its blueprint, then other filled fields. Add two sections at the end, each only when there is something to show. Relations: read project.relations.list(ticket.id). For each relation print one line with the other ticket's key, title and status, grouped as 'blocked by' (type blocks and this ticket is the target), 'blocks' (type blocks and this ticket is the source) and, for every other type, the type name with underscores replaced by spaces (for example 'relates to'). Get the other ticket with project.tickets.get(id). Code plan: the ticket record has a field codePlan with the lists implements, consumes and changes; each entry names a component id. The command heist codeplan show in the same file shows how to get the resolved names: project.context(id, {budget: 1e9}) returns codePlan with name and kind per entry. Print one line per entry, for example 'consumes relationGraph (function)   heist contract show relationGraph', and for consumes also the required fields if the entry has requires. Keep --format json unchanged: it prints the raw ticket.
why: A person or agent reading a ticket does not see that a contract is attached or what the ticket waits for; both live outside the ticket record.

acceptance.text: heist ticket show prints blockers, blocked tickets and other relations with key, title and status
It prints the code plan with component names
Tickets without relations or code plan look as before
